what: Documented the shallow URL-state pattern used to make /data tabs URL-addressable.
why: The pattern (SvelteKit shallow routing helper + no-op guard + clean-default stripping) is reusable for any filter/tab/panel state that should survive reload or be shareable.
summary: Recorded learning `shallow-url-state-sveltekit-replacestate`: sync view state (e.g. /data tabs) to the URL with `replaceState` from `$app/navigation` inside a guarded `$effect` — never `goto()` (re-runs loads, spams history) or raw `window.history.replaceState` (desyncs `page.url`). Strip the param on the default value; consume-once presets (add=1) are stripped at init so they never fight the tab writer. Renamed file to shorten a W2 warning; validate now clean.

user: Dev restarts on Windows now avoid silent command mangling — fewer false "the fix doesn't work" loops caused by broken kill/relaunch commands
what: Documented a Windows-shell gotcha hit while restarting the dev app: Git Bash (MSYS) rewrites flags like `/f` into paths (`F:/`), so kill/relaunch commands silently break; fix is MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 or PowerShell, and always kill by specific PID.
why: The restart chain is the standard way to rule out stale webviews; when its commands silently mangle, debugging wastes a full loop chasing a bug that no longer exists.
next: See docs/wiki/learnings/msys-path-conversion-mangles-f-style-windows-flags-use-msys-.md before running taskkill/start from bash
summary: Recorded a learning from the /data tab URL-sync debugging session: MSYS path conversion silently rewrites `/f`-style Windows flags into drive paths (use `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` or PowerShell), plus the practice of killing app/vite by specific PID instead of blanket `taskkill /IM node.exe /f`.

user: Charts wired to master items (measures/dimensions) now actually render — every one of them was silently broken before
what: Fixed two bugs that made every master-item-based chart fail with "no relationship path" or "unknown column": a tableName/table field mismatch between the Rust backend and the frontend, and expression-based master dimensions (like year(order_date)) being rejected by the query compiler. Verified end-to-end: the Sales Overview page builds, persists, and renders (bar chart with 5 bars, table with 50 rows).
why: The semantic layer (master items) is the core of report building — until this fix, any chart using a saved measure or dimension could not draw at all, while raw-field charts worked, making the failure look like a data problem rather than a plumbing bug.
next: Open /pages, wire a chart to your ⭐ master items — it renders now. Open findings are tracked in reports/pages-e2e-feedback.md

user: Hung saves now fail fast with a clear error and auto-retry — your edits can no longer vanish silently
what: Validation and save operations in the page editor and item editor now time out (15–20s) with an honest error message, and failed writes automatically retry once. Previously a backend hang left "checking…" on screen forever and silently dropped saves.
why: A backend hang used to swallow saves without any signal — page blocks appeared to "vanish" and validation spun eternally.
next: Edit charts and save as usual — hangs now surface as clear errors instead of spinning forever.

user: The app no longer freezes after certain failed queries — the database connection now self-recovers in about a second instead of needing an app restart
what: The backend now detects the Windows DuckDB "poisoned connection" bug (duckdb-rs #209): when a query hits it, the backend drops and reopens the connection and retries the query once, all in-process. The P1 "app hang" from the /pages E2E report is cured at the root; the same-day frontend timeout/retry safety net stays in place.
why: A wedged connection used to mean a silently frozen app and a manual restart, throwing away whatever the user was doing.
next: Just use the app — failed queries recover on their own now. Details: docs/wiki/learnings/duckdb-app-hangs-poisoned-connection-on-windows-duckdb-rs-20.md
